description: Quad buffer as LED data level shifter
notes: SOIC-14. 5V rail TTL thresholds so 3V3 reads high. Two spare gates - CONFIRMED SPARE 2026-09-21: the WS2815 datasheet's own recommended application circuit GROUNDS the first pixel's BI (L1 pin 6 to pin 5), so only DI needs driving on each run. WS2815 THRESHOLD VERIFIED: V_IH = 0.7 x VDD in a table whose header declares VDD = 4.5-5.5V, so 3.15-3.85V, which this part clears at 5V. The 8.4V figure that worried three documents came from substituting the +12V LED rail into that table

description: HF decoupling at every carrier IC - ADC, reference, buffer, level shifter, sensor
notes: One per supply pin: MCP3202, REF5050 IN AND OUT, OPA2197 +12V, 74AHCT125, MPXV4006DP, and both R-78E5 inputs. ADR 0001 fixed only the shift registers (C-DECOUPLE-165) and stopped there | 2026-09-21: QTY 7 -> 8. The old enumeration gave the REF5050 one 100nF while carrier.md drew one at its OUTPUT and the prose claimed one at the sensor's VS pin - the same part spent twice across three files, and none drawn at VS at all. SBOS410O section 9.4.1.1 pp.29-30 wants both: a VIN bypass AND 'a high-frequency, 1uF capacitor in parallel between the output and ground'. Settled allocation is REF5050 VIN, REF5050 VOUT, and SKT-BREATH VS - and the VS one is the 100 nF the reference buffer's compensation is designed against. See figures.yaml cref-out-node

description: Series resistor on each WS2815 data line at the driver
notes: TWO PARTS ON THE AGGRESSOR, against 63 on the victims. Standard practice at an addressable-LED driver: damps the fastest edge in the instrument at its source and protects the 74AHCT125 output. TWO, NOT FOUR - reverted 2026-09-21. This row went to four on the reasoning that the WS2815's BACKUP data line was connected to nothing and the level shifter's two spare gates were exactly what it needed. The datasheet (datasheets/led/WS2815.pdf) shows the vendor's own recommended circuit GROUNDING the first pixel's BI (L1 pin 6 to pin 5); from L2 onward BI comes from the PREVIOUS pixel's DI, internal to the tape, which is what makes the backup line lag by one and lets a dead pixel be bypassed. The head of the strip has nothing to lag. So BI is a ground connection, not a driven one: two gates, two resistors, and the LED loom stays at 6 conductors rather than 8. The figure is a raster with no text layer and was read by rendering at 700dpi - confirm visually before crimping
